newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA UPBEAT ON 10 PCT MOBILE MARGINS.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA UPBEAT ON 10 PCT MOBILE MARGINS.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said on Thursday it was confident of holding mobile phone margins above 10 percent in 1997.
"Our target for this year is at least 10 percent. We feel good about achieving that," CEO Jorma Ollila told a news conference after Nokia reported its 1996 results.
On telecommunications, Ollila said the company did not see any major change in the growth picture this year.

"We don't see any significant change in the picture for 1997," he said, referring to 30 percent sales growth in telecommunications and the fact Nokia was almost able to match price erosion by increasing productivity.
Ollila said Nokia's mobile phone margins were about 13 percent in the second half of the year, with mobile phones' profitability only achieved in that period.
"The fourth quarter was stronger than the third," he said.
Asked if Nokia had lost market share to any rivals, such as Sweden's Ericsson or Motorola of the U.S., he said: "I don't think we have lost to anybody."
